subsystems.name: NAND flash memory
subsystems.role: stores data as electrical charge in microscopic cells.

subsystems.name: Controller
subsystems.role: the brain that manages every read, write and erase.

subsystems.name: Firmware
subsystems.role: decides where data goes and keeps the drive healthy.

subsystems.name: PCB and power delivery
subsystems.role: the physical board that connects all chips and feeds them stable power.
parts: M.2 or U.2 printed circuit board

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: keeps the controller and NAND cool enough to run at full speed.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate NAND wafers
buildSteps.detail: Alternating layers of oxide and nitride are deposited, deep holes are etched, and charge-trap material and vertical channels are formed; metal wiring is added on top.

buildSteps.title: Test and dice wafers
buildSteps.detail: Every die is probed electrically; good ones are cut from the wafer.

buildSteps.title: Stack and package NAND dies
buildSteps.detail: Multiple dies are stacked vertically, connected by wire bonds or through-silicon vias, then encapsulated in a protective package.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate controller chip
buildSteps.detail: The controller is designed on an advanced logic process, fabricated on wafers, tested and diced.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the SSD
buildSteps.detail: Controller, NAND packages, optional DRAM and passive components are surface-mounted onto a printed circuit board.

buildSteps.title: Load firmware and test
buildSteps.detail: Firmware is flashed, the drive is calibrated, and full read/write tests are run across its capacity.

buildSteps.title: Final assembly and labelling
buildSteps.detail: A heat spreader or label is attached, and the drive is tested again before packing.

prerequisites.why: stacks hundreds of layers so capacity grows without shrinking cells to unreliable sizes.
controllers need fast, low-power logic to handle PCIe speeds and error correction.
they define the physical link and the command protocol between host and SSD.
flash cells wear out and produce errors; LDPC corrects them to keep data readable.
drivers and file systems must issue NVMe commands and manage TRIM for long life.

pathway.milestone: PCIe 4.0/5.0 NVMe SSDs using 3D NAND with over 200 layers
pathway.unlocks: fast boot and application loading for most computers.

pathway.milestone: PCIe 6.0 links and higher layer counts (300+), plus QLC and PLC storage
pathway.unlocks: cheaper, denser storage for data centres.
offloading data processing and expanding memory pools.

pathway.milestone: New non-volatile memories such as MRAM or ReRAM complementing NAND
pathway.unlocks: faster, more durable storage tiers in the memory hierarchy.
